questions.educationalObjective: Generate the panic disorder treatment plan.

exhibits.title: Plan
exhibits.body: Sertraline 25 mg daily, increase slowly. Lorazepam 0.5 mg as needed for 2 weeks. CBT referral.

questions.stem: Which teaching should the nurse give about the new medicines? Select all that apply.

options.text: Sertraline may take 4 to 6 weeks to work
Anxiety may briefly worsen at the start of sertraline
Do not drink alcohol with lorazepam
Do not stop lorazepam suddenly after regular use
Take extra lorazepam before driving to prevent attacks
Stop sertraline once you feel better after a week

rationale.correct: Delayed SSRI effect, avoiding alcohol and not stopping suddenly.
references: Nursing pharmacology texts (e.g. Lehne; McCuistion) and the drug's prescribing information
Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026.

rows.text: One mild attack this month (was several a week)

"I cut down to one coffee a day."
"I take lorazepam every day now, sometimes three tablets."
"I use slow breathing when I feel it starting."

rationale.correct: Fewer attacks and less avoidance; daily benzodiazepine use needs review.

caseStudies.title: Post-traumatic stress disorder in a veteran

exhibits.title: Veterans clinic

The veteran has nightmares most nights, startles at loud noises, avoids crowds and fireworks, and says, "I feel numb, like I'm watching my life on TV." The veteran drinks 8 beers most nights to sleep. The veteran's partner reports angry outbursts.
